# Temple Scroll Column 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 18 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**18:1** And you shall wash them with water.

**18:2** And you shall take the garments and clothe Aaron with the tunic and the robe of the ephod

**18:3** and the ephod and the breastpiece, and you shall fasten upon him the band of the ephod.

**18:4** And you shall set the turban upon his head and put the holy diadem upon the turban.

**18:5** And you shall take the anointing oil and pour it upon his head and anoint him.

**18:6** And his sons you shall bring near and clothe them with tunics.

**18:7** And you shall gird them with sashes, Aaron and his sons, and bind headbands upon them.

**18:8** And the priesthood shall be theirs by a perpetual statute. And you shall ordain Aaron and his sons.

**18:9** And you shall bring near the bull before the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the bull.

**18:10** And you shall slaughter the bull before Me, before the tent of meeting.

**18:11** And you shall take from the blood of the bull and put it upon the horns of the altar with your finger.

**18:12** And all the remaining blood you shall pour out at the base of the altar.

**18:13** And you shall take all the fat that covers the entrails and the lobe upon the liver

**18:14** and the two kidneys and the fat that is upon them, and you shall make them smoke upon the altar.

**18:15** But the flesh of the bull and its skin and its dung you shall burn with fire outside the camp; it is a sin offering.

---

*EMET notes: Column 18 is well preserved. It continues the ordination (millu'im) instructions, paralleling Exodus 29:4-14. The sequence follows: ritual washing, vesting of Aaron (tunic, robe, ephod, breastpiece, turban, diadem), anointing with oil, vesting of his sons, hand-laying on the bull, slaughter, blood manipulation (horns of the altar and base), fat portions burned on the altar, remainder burned outside the camp. "Make them smoke" (hiqtir) preserves the technical sacrificial term distinct from "burn" (saraf).*
